class=\"two-col-container container\">\r\n        <div class=\"row\">\r\n            <div class=\"col-md-12 col-lg-8\">\r\n                \r\n<header class=\"container\">\r\n    <div class=\"page-heading\">\r\n<h1>Burke-Gilman Trail</h1>    </div>\r\n</header>\r\n            </div>\r\n            <aside class=\"col-md-12 col-lg-4 right-rail\">\r\n                \r\n            </aside>\r\n        </div>\r\n    </div>\r\n</div>\r\n        </div>\r\n        <div class=\"\">\r\n            \r\n\r\n\r\n<div class=\" pt-medium pb-small  \">\r\n    <div class=\"two-col-container container\">\r\n        <div class=\"row\">\r\n            <div class=\"col-md-12 col-lg-8\">\r\n                \r\n\r\n<div class=\"basic-image  \">\r\n    <figure>\r\n\r\n\r\n        <img src=\"https://cdn.kingcounty.gov/-/media/king-county/depts/dnrp/nature-recreation/parks-recreation/trails/leafline-trails/burke-gilman/burkegilman.png?h=192&amp;iar=0&amp;w=770&amp;rev=00566ad88ddb450f81ee0ba25d6bf865&amp;hash=CFDD1F47B945273B052BCA258E7230EA\" class=\"rounded-0 img-fluid\" alt=\"\" width=\"770\" height=\"192\" />\r\n\r\n    </figure>\r\n</div>\r\n\r\n            </div>\r\n            <aside class=\"col-md-12 col-lg-4 right-rail\">\r\n                \r\n            </aside>\r\n        </div>\r\n    </div>\r\n</div>\r\n\r\n\r\n<div class=\" pt-medium pb-large  \">\r\n    <div class=\"two-col-container container\">\r\n        <div class=\"row\">\r\n            <div class=\"col-md-12 col-lg-8\">\r\n                \r\n\r\n\r\n<div class=\"rich-text\"><h2>About the Trail</h2>\n<p>The Burke-Gilman Trail (BGT) runs more than 20 miles from Shilshole Bay in the City of Seattle to the City of Bothell where it intersects the Sammamish River Trail. Part of the \"Locks to Lakes Corridor,\" the BGT is a paved, off-road facility over its entire length with the exception of an on-road segment in Ballard. </p>\n<p>The trail crosses Ballard, Fremont, Wallingford, the University District and View Ridge within the City of Seattle, as well as the cities of Lake Forest Park, Kenmore and Bothell. The trail is managed by Seattle within the city limits south of Northeast 145th Street and by King County outside Seattle.</p>\n<p>The trail follows a historic railroad route near the Lake Washington Ship Canal and north along Lake Washington to the Sammamish River. Along the way it passes the Hiram Chittenden Locks, Fremont Canal Park, Gas Works Park, University of Washington, Magnuson Park, Log Boom Park in Kenmore, Wayne Golf Course in Bothell and Blyth Park in Bothell. </p>\n<p>King County's best-known regional trail, the BGT is highly popular with cyclists, joggers, skaters and strollers. It is also an important nonmotorized route for weekday bicycle commuters between Seattle and the Eastside. The trail provides great access and views of the Ship Canal, Lake Union, Seattle neighborhoods, suburban cities, Lake Washington, and points east via other regional trails.</p></div>\r\n            </div>\r\n            <aside class=\"col-md-12 col-lg-4 right-rail\">\r\n                \r\n<div class=\"box test\">\r\n                    <h2 class=\"box-title \">Quick facts</h2>\r\n\r\n    \r\n    <p><strong>Length:</strong> 20.0 miles. </p>\n<p><strong>Surface:</strong>&nbsp;Paved with soft surface shoulder (Seattle and King County).</p>\n<p><strong>Use:</strong> All non-motorized uses are permitted except equestrians.</p>\n<p><strong>Access:</strong> Gasworks Park, Matthews Beach Park, Log Boom Park.</p>\n<p><strong>Accessibility:</strong> The trail is ADA accessible. Disability access at: Gasworks Park and Log Boom Park.</p>\r\n</div>\r\n\r\n\r\n            </aside>\r\n        </div>\r\n    </div>\r\n</div>\r\n\r\n\r\n<section class=\"topic-cards-row\">\r\n </nav>\r\n</div>\r\n    <main id=\"maincontent\" class=\"add-scroll-top-margin\">\r\n\r\n        <div class=\"\">\r\n            \r\n            \r\n\r\n\r\n<div class=\"    \">\r\n    <div class=\"two-col-container container\">\r\n        <div class=\"row\">\r\n            <div class=\"col-md-12 col-lg-8\">\r\n                \r\n<header class=\"container\">\r\n    <div class=\"page-heading\">\r\n<h1>Sammamish River Trail</h1>    </div>\r\n</header>\r\n            </div>\r\n            <aside class=\"col-md-12 col-lg-4 right-rail\">\r\n                \r\n            </aside>\r\n        </div>\r\n    </div>\r\n</div>\r\n        </div>\r\n        <div class=\"\">\r\n            \r\n\r\n\r\n<div class=\"  pb-medium  \">\r\n    <div class=\"two-col-container container\">\r\n        <div class=\"row\">\r\n            <div class=\"col-md-12 col-lg-8\">\r\n                \r\n\r\n<div class=\"basic-image  \">\r\n    <figure>\r\n\r\n\r\n        <img src=\"https://cdn.kingcounty.gov/-/media/king-county/depts/dnrp/nature-recreation/parks-recreation/trails/leafline-trails/sammamish-river-trail/sammamishrivertrail.png?h=200&amp;iar=0&amp;w=800&amp;rev=a0197f36331d4c11a415fbb7b0ec8291&amp;hash=D363C7ABB5A15B55FA1B6A9E4E2DB722\" class=\"rounded-0 img-fluid\" alt=\"Cyclists ride towards and away from the viewer along the paved trail bordered in tall green grasses\" width=\"800\" height=\"200\" />\r\n\r\n    </figure>\r\n</div>\r\n\r\n            </div>\r\n            <aside class=\"col-md-12 col-lg-4 right-rail\">\r\n                \r\n            </aside>\r\n        </div>\r\n    </div>\r\n</div>\r\n\r\n\r\n<div class=\" pt-medium pb-medium  \">\r\n    <div class=\"two-col-container container\">\r\n        <div class=\"row\">\r\n            <div class=\"col-md-12 col-lg-8\">\r\n                \r\n\r\n\r\n<div class=\"rich-text\"><p><span class=\"h2\">About the Trail</span></p>\n<p>The Sammamish River Trail runs 10.1 miles along the Sammamish River from Bothell to Marymoor Park in Redmond as part of the “Locks to Lakes Corridor.</p>\n<p>The SRT is paved its entire length and is one of King County’s most popular regional trails. The trail offers extraordinary views of the river, the broad Sammamish River Valley, Cascade foothills and Mt. Rainier. Bicyclists, joggers, skaters, walkers, and others enjoy the trail as a regional recreation resource.</p>\n<p>The SRT is also used extensively by commuters as a non-motorized corridor between suburban cities and Seattle. A separate soft-surface path runs parallel to the trail between Woodinville and Marymoor Park and provides access for equestrians.</p>\n<p>Starting at its intersection with the Burke-Gilman Trail near Blyth Park in the City of Bothell, the SRT continues east and south through Woodinville and Redmond, passing Bothell Landing, Sammamish River Park, Wilmot Gateway Park in Woodinville, Northshore Athletic Fields, Woodinville’s wineries and breweries, Sixty Acres Park, and Redmond City Hall before entering King County’s Marymoor Park. The Marymoor Connector Trail connects the trail with the East Lake Sammamish Trail via Marymoor Park. The trail also provides access to the Power Line and the Bear Creek Trails in Redmond.</p></div>\r\n            </div>\r\n            <aside class=\"col-md-12 col-lg-4 right-rail\">\r\n                \r\n<div class=\"box test\">\r\n                    <h2 class=\"box-title \">Quick facts about this trail</h2>\r\n\r\n    \r\n    <p><strong>Length</strong>: 10.1 miles. Surface - Paved with soft surface shoulder.</p>\n<p><strong>Use</strong>: Equestrians are allowed on the Sammamish River Trail between NE 175th St in Woodinville to Marymoor Park and a separate soft surface equestrian trail exists. All other non-motorized uses are permitted on the trail.</p>\n<p><strong>Accessibility</strong>: The trail is ADA accessible except for two short sections that have grades below standards (one located just east of 96th Ave NE in Bothell, and the other located just north of NE 145th St. Disability access at: Wilmot Park and Redmond City Hall.</p>\n<p><strong>Access</strong>: Blyth Park, Bothell Landing, Jerry Wilmot Park, 60-Acre Park, and Marymoor Park.</p>\r\n</div>\r\n\r\n\r\n            </aside>\r\n        </div>\r\n    </div>\r\n</div>\r\n\r\n\r\n<section class=\"topic-cards-row\">\r\n class=\"vital-wrapper\" id=\"vitalInfoHeading-204d77f977b94f18a32ff17115cbb30d\">\r\n        <h2 class='vital-info-heading'>King County Parks</h2>\r\n        \r\n        <div class=\"rich-text\"><p>Email: parksinfo@kingcounty.gov</p>\n<hr />\n<p>Phone: 206-477-4527</p>\n<p>Call 711 to be connected to the Washington Relay Service</p>\n<hr />\n<p>Customer Service Hours: 8:30 am to 4:30 pm, Monday through Friday</p>\n<hr />\n<p>After Hours: 206-477-8100</p>\n<hr />\n<p>Media Coordination: <a href=\"/en/dept/dnrp/about-king-county/about-dnrp/newsroom\">DNRP Newsroom</a></p>\n<hr />\n<p>Mailing Address: 201 S Jackson Street, KSC-NR-6500, Seattle, WA 98104</p></div>\r\n    </div>\r\n</aside>\r\n            </aside>\r\n        </div>\r\n    </div>\r\n</div>\r\n        </div>\r\n        <div class=\"\">\r\n            \r\n\r\n<aside class=\"highlight-banner highlight-banner-primary\" aria-labelledby=\"ELST-closure-starting-June-1,-2026-title\">\r\n    <div class=\"container\">\r\n        <div class=\"row align-items-center\">\r\n\r\n                        <h2 class=\"col-sm-4 highlight-banner-title h3\" id=\"ELST-closure-starting-June-1,-2026-title\">\r\n                            ELST closure starting June 1, 2026\r\n                        </h2>\r\n\r\n            <div class=\"col highlight-banner-text\">\r\n                <div class=\"rich-text\"><p>A section of the East Lake Sammamish Trail will be closed starting June 1, 2026 and last through the rest of the year so crews can replace aging culverts.&nbsp;<a href=\"https://kingcounty.gov/en/dept/dnrp/nature-recreation/parks-recreation/king-county-parks/trails/leafline-trails/east-lake-sammamish/#elst-closure-anchor-link\">Learn more below.</a></p></div>\r\n            </div>\r\n\r\n\r\n            <div class=\"col-sm-2 highlight-banner-link\">\r\n\r\n                \r\n            </div>\r\n\r\n        </div>\r\n    </div>\r\n</aside>\r\n\r\n\r\n<div class=\" pt-medium pb-large border-bottom-overcast \">\r\n    <div class=\"two-col-container container\">\r\n        <div class=\"row\">\r\n            <div class=\"col-md-12 col-lg-8\">\r\n                \r\n\r\n\r\n<div class=\"rich-text\"><h2>About the trail</h2>\n<p>The East Lake Sammamish Trail (ELST) is an 11-mile, fully paved waterfront trail that offers a scenic connection between Redmond, Sammamish, and Issaquah. It forms a key link in the 44-mile paved Locks to Lake Corridor, which stretches all the way from Seattle’s Ballard waterfront to Eastside communities and the Cascade foothills. </p>\n<p>Along its southern end in Issaquah, the ELST connects directly to King County’s Issaquah–Preston Trail. At the north end, the trail meets the Marymoor Connector Trail in Marymoor Park and continues north on the Redmond Central Connector Trail to Redmond Town Center, providing seamless access to the Sammamish River Trail and to Sound Transit’s Link light rail stations in Redmond. </p>\n<p>King County Parks purchased the 11-mile East Lake Sammamish corridor in 1997, opening a narrower, gravel-surfaced interim trail in 2006. Fully developed trail segments were completed in Redmond in 2011, in Issaquah two years later, and Sammamish in 2015,  2018, and 2023. </p></div>\r\n            </div>\r\n            <aside class=\"col-md-12 col-lg-4 right-rail\">\r\n                \r\n<div class=\"box test\">\r\n                    <h3 class=\"box-title \">Quick Facts</h3>\r\n\r\n    \r\n    <p><strong>Length:</strong> 11 miles. </p>\n<p><strong>Surface: </strong>12-foot wide paved trail with soft (gravel) shoulders.</p>\n<p><strong>Use:</strong> All non-motorized uses. Speed limit 15 mph. </p>\n<p><strong>Major access points:</strong> </p>\n<ul>\n    <li>NE 70th Street parking area (Redmond) </li>\n    <li>NE 65th Street parking area (Redmond) </li>\n    <li>187th Avenue NE (Redmond) </li>\n    <li>NE Inglewood Hill Rd parking area (Sammamish) </li>\n    <li>Louis Thompson Road ramp (Sammamish) </li>\n    <li>SE 8th Street  </li>\n    <li>SE 33rd Street  </li>\n    <li>212th Way SE and SE 43rd Way (Sammamish) </li>\n    <li>SE 51st, 56th, 62nd Streets (Issaquah) </li>\n    <li>NW Gilman Boulevard (Issaquah) </li>\n</ul>\n<p />\n<p><strong>Accessibility:</strong> The trail is ADA accessible. </p>\r\n</div>\r\n\r\n\r\n            </aside>\r\n        </div>\r\n    </div>\r\n</div>\r\n\r\n\r\n<div class=\" pt-large pb-large border-bottom-overcast \">\r\n    <div class=\"two-col-container container\">\r\n        <div class=\"row\">\r\n            <div class=\"col-md-12 col-lg-8\">\r\n                \r\n<span id=\"elst-closure-anchor-link\" data-toc-anchor=\"elst-closure-anchor-link\"></span>\r\n\r\n\r\n\r\n\r\n\r\n<div class=\"rich-text\"><h2>ELST closure beginning June 1 2026&nbsp;</h2>\n<p>A section of the East Lake Sammamish Trail (ELST) will be closed starting June 1, 2026 and last through the rest of the year so crews can replace aging culverts under the ELST. </p>\n<p>Although the construction area is short, its location will temporarily split the trail into two separate sections. There will be no detour around the construction closure. <a rel=\"noopener noreferrer\" href=\"https://www.google.com/maps/place/47%C2%B037'02.8%22N+122%C2%B004'04.5%22W/@47.619504,-122.067352,743m/data=!3m1!1e3!4m12!1m7!3m6!1s0x549071f59f788779:0xf896c35240e89940!2sThe+Knolls+at+Inglewood+Hill!8m2!3d47.6157068!4d-122.038144!16s%2Fg%2F1hc3g1hm1!3m3!8m2!3d47.617432!4d-122.06792?entry=ttu&amp;g_ep=EgoyMDI2MDMwOS4wIKXMDSoASAFQAw%3D%3D\" target=\"_blank\">The 600 ft trail closure area is located between Louis Thompson Rd NE and NE Inglewood Hill Rd.</a> </p>\n<p>Once the culverts under the trail have been completed a new wide paved trail section will be built.  </p>\n<p>Once complete, this will open high‑quality salmon habitat on George Davis Creek and finish the last section of the ELST. </p>\n<p>Thank you for your patience as we work to help recover local Kokanee salmon populations. </p>\n<p>Learn more about the <a rel=\"noopener noreferrer\" href=\"https://www.sammamish.us/projects/george-davis-creek-fish-passage-and-storm-improvement-project/\" target=\"_blank\">City of Sammamish&rsquo;s partnering culvert project</a> including <a rel=\"noopener noreferrer\" href=\"https://www.sammamish.us/i-want-to/cone-zone/\" target=\"_blank\"><span>Cone Zone, where subscribers can get weekly updates on road work in Sammamish</span></a>.</p></div>\r\n            </div>\r\n            <aside class=\"col-md-12 col-lg-4 right-rail\">\r\n                \r\n\r\n<div class=\"basic-image  \">\r\n    <figure>\r\n\r\n<br />\r\n        <img src=\"https://cdn.kingcounty.gov/-/media/king-county/depts/dnrp/nature-recreation/parks-recreation/trails/leafline-trails/east-lake-sammamish/elst-2026-closure-map.png?h=1486&amp;iar=0&amp;w=1019&amp;rev=d0f92b3c2b85488983fa943b5343367a&amp;hash=24CDC32603C501F6B2C3C8E8081F678B\" class=\" img-fluid\" alt=\"A map of the East Lake Sammamish Trail with a detail area showing the 600 ft trail closure area between Louis Thompson Rd NE and NE Inglewood Hill Rd with a red line.\" width=\"1019\" height=\"1486\" />\r\n\r\n            <figcaption>A map of the East Lake Sammamish Trail with a detail area showing the 600 ft trail closure area between Louis Thompson Rd NE and NE Inglewood Hill Rd marked with a red line.</figcaption>\r\n    </figure>\r\n</div>\r\n\r\n            </aside>\r\n        </div>\r\n    </div>\r\n</div>\r\n\r\n\r\n<div class=\" pt-medium pb-large  \">\r\n    <div class=\"two-col-container container\">\r\n        <div class=\"row\">\r\n            <div class=\"col-md-12 col-lg-8\">\r\n                \r\n\r\n\r\n<div class=\"rich-text\"><p><span class=\"h2\">Trail history</span></p>\n<p><span class=\"h3\">The trail a half-century in the making</span></p>\n<p>The East Lake Sammamish rail corridor (ELSRC) was built in 1889 as part of a rail line running from Seattle to the coal mines in what is now Issaquah. Over time, the corridor changed owners several times, with Burlington Northern Santa Fe (BNSF) as the final rail operator. </p>\n<p>In 1997, BNSF chose to stop using the line and sold the corridor to the Cascade Land Conservancy and King County. King County had already identified this section as an important future part of the Regional Trails System. In 1998, the U.S. Surface Transportation Board approved the County’s request to “railbank” the corridor, which protects it for possible future development while allowing it to be used as a trail. That same year, the Cascade Land Conservancy transferred its interest in the corridor to King County. </p>\n<p>In 2000, the King County Council approved funding to build a soft surface trail along the corridor. King County Parks worked with communities across the region to develop the East Lake Sammamish Trail Master Plan. After resolving legal challenges, the interim trail opened in 2006. Fully developed trail segments were completed in Redmond (2011), Issaquah (2013), and Sammamish (2015, and 2018, and 2023). </p>\n<div style=\"padding:56.25% 0 0 0;position:relative;\"><iframe src=\"https://player.vimeo.com/video/873093461?badge=0&autopause=0&player_id=0&app_id=58479\" frameborder=\"0\" allow=\"autoplay; fullscreen; picture-in-picture; clipboard-write; encrypted-media; web-share\" referrerpolicy=\"strict-origin-when-cross-origin\" style=\"position:absolute;top:0;left:0;width:100%;height:100%;\" title=\"The East Lake Sammamish Trail is ready to ride\"></iframe></div></div>\r\n            </div>\r\n            <aside class=\"col-md-12 col-lg-4 right-rail\">\r\n                \r\n            </aside>\r\n        </div>\r\n Green plants and trees line the banks, and a wooden fence is visible in the background.\" />\r\n            </figure>\r\n\r\n<p>For information regarding possible delays on E. Lake Sammamish Pkwy, the City's <a href=\"/i-want-to/cone-zone/\" title=\"Cone Zone\">Cone Zone</a> web page will be updated weekly when construction begins.  For information relating to ELS Trail closure, visit King County's web page <a href=\"https://kingcounty.gov/en/dept/dnrp/nature-recreation/parks-recreation/king-county-parks/trails/leafline-trails/east-lake-sammamish/#elst-closure-anchor-link\" title=\"King County-East Lake Sammamish Trail\" data-anchor=\"#elst-closure-anchor-link\">East Lake Sammamish Trail.</a></p>\n<p>If you are concerned about possible traffic delays in this corridor, it is recommended that you utilize the detour map below.</p>\n<p><img src=\"/media/uoqgjt24/detour-map.jpg?width=485.6927710843373&amp;height=500\" alt=\"\" width=\"485.6927710843373\" height=\"500\"></p>\r\n\r\n\r\n   <div class=\"gov-delivery\">\r\n    <a class=\"btn action action--govDelivery no-external-icon\" href=\"https://service.govdelivery.com/accounts/WASAMMAM/subscriber/new?topic_id=WASAMMAM_141\" target=\"_blank\" rel=\"noopener noreferrer\" aria-label=\"Subscribe (opens in a new window)\">\r\n        <span class=\"action--icon\" aria-hidden=\"true\">mail</span>\r\n        <span>Subscribe</span>\r\n    </a>\r\n    </div>\r\n\r\n<h2>Overview</h2>\n<p>The first day of construction is planned for June 1, 2026. The first items of work will be off East Lake Sammamish Shore Lane NE, in the vicinity of the King County Parks Trail. Then the project will include East Lake Sammamish Parkway, private property work, and stream corridor reconstruction. During the full closure, major utility relocations and partial bridge construction will occur. Concurrently, stream restoration and pile drilling will be ongoing until complete. The in-water-work window will be from June 15th until October 31st per the City's hydraulic project permit. Once stream restoration is complete, the stream bypass will be removed and the full flow of George Davis Creek will return all the way to Lake Sammamish. </p>\n<h3>Background</h3>\n<p>The Public Works Department initiated the George Davis Creek project in 2018 to address problems with the aging drainage system near the stream's approach to East Lake Sammamish Parkway. Residents and staff identified multiple concerns including:</p>\n<ul>\n<li>\n<p>Periodic flooding near the East Lake Sammamish Regional Trail and the Parkway.</p>\n</li>\n<li>\n<p>Costly annual maintenance to clear the high-flow bypass of stream sediment.</p>\n</li>\n<li>\n<p>Replacement needs as the system approaches the end of its predicted lifecycle.</p>\n</li>\n<li>\n<p>Multiple barriers to fish passage for migrating kokanee salmon and other salmonoids.</p>\n</li>\n</ul>\n<p>In 2019, the City identified a preferred option to replace the existing drainage system with an open stream channel. The project corridor would extend from Lake Sammamish 900 feet east to a point where George Davis Creek flows through an undisturbed, pristine ravine.</p>\n<h3>Location</h3>\n<p><img src=\"/media/4dveosvs/vicinity-map.png?mode=crop&amp;width=500\" alt=\"\" width=\"500\" height=\"332.81853281853284\"></p>\r\n\r\n\r\n<h3>Design Focus</h3>\n<p>Project design is governed by the State Hydraulic Code (<a rel=\"noopener\" href=\"https://app.leg.wa.gov/WAC/default.aspx/default.aspx?cite=220-660\" target=\"_blank\" data-anchor=\"?cite=220-660\">WAC 220-660</a>) which requires any drainage improvements in a stream to consider passage for both resident and migratory fish. In response to these rules, project designers have devoted significant attention to ensuring the proposed improvements remove existing fish passage barriers.</p>\n<p>A schematic map of the <a rel=\"noopener\" href=\"/media/ctiocdg2/ex-fish-passage-barriers.pdf\" target=\"_blank\" title=\"Ex Fish Passage Barriers\">existing barriers</a> illustrates the extent of the work needed to connect Lake Sammamish to the high quality stream habitat located 900 feet east of the lake. The <a rel=\"noopener\" href=\"/media/rpuhtslj/proposed-stream-improvements.pdf\" target=\"_blank\" title=\"Proposed Stream Improvements\">proposed stream</a> will eliminate these barriers and reestablish the stream through the developed lakeside corridor around East Lake Sammamish Parkway.</p>\r\n\r\n\r\n<h3>Partnerships</h3>\n<p>This project's success reflects cooperation with several regional groups and the broader community. The following organizations have offered significant support to this project:</p>\n<ul>\n<li><a rel=\"noopener\" href=\"https://kingcounty.gov/en/dept/dnrp/nature-recreation/environment-ecology-conservation/wildlife/fish-and-shellfish/kokanee/kokanee-workgroup\" target=\"_blank\">Kokanee Work Group</a></li>\n<li><a rel=\"noopener\" href=\"https://www.threeriverstu.org/\" target=\"_blank\">Trout Unlimited</a></li>\n<li><a rel=\"noopener\" href=\"https://www.govlink.org/watersheds/8/committees/default.aspx\" target=\"_blank\">WRIA 8 Salmon Recovery Council</a></li>\n<li><a rel=\"noopener\" href=\"https://enr.snoqualmietribe.us/tag/kokanee/\" target=\"_blank\">Snoqualmie Indian Tribe</a></li>\n</ul>\n<p>King County Department of Natural Resources and Parks remains a critical partner in this project. Final improvements to the <a href=\"https://www.kingcounty.gov/services/parks-recreation/parks/trails/regional-trails/popular-trails/east-lake-samm.aspx\">East Lake Sammamish Regional Trail</a> require the County to replace the culverts that route George Davis Creek beneath the trail.  Additionally, King County will replace the culvert beneath East Lake Sammamish Shore Lane NE.</p>\n<h3>Kokanee Salmon</h3>\n<p><img src=\"/media/edplgagf/fish4.jpg?mode=crop&amp;width=500&amp;height=375\" alt=\"\" width=\"500\" height=\"375\"></p>\n<p>Lake Sammamish is home to a population of native kokanee salmon. This variant of sockeye salmon does not migrate to oceans but instead spends its adult life in freshwater lakes. The kokanee population unique to Lake Sammamish remains threatened by changing lake conditions, reduced access to spawning streams, invasive predator fish, and other pressures.</p>\n<p>The Kokanee Work Group (KWG) formed in 2007 to prevent the extinction and improve the health of this native kokanee population. Through the <a rel=\"noopener\" href=\"https://your.kingcounty.gov/dnrp/library/water-and-land/salmon/kokanee/kokanee-workgroup/front-matter-kokanee-blueprint.pdf\" target=\"_blank\">Blueprint for the Restoration and Enhancement of Lake Sammamish Kokanee Tributaries</a>, the KWG recognized the value of historic spawning streams to kokanee survival. This project seeks to achieve that goal.</p>\n<p>In addition to creating 900 feet of potential spawning habitat where none now exists, the project will provide unimpeded access to an additional 2,000 feet of high quality stream upstream of the project corridor. </p>\n<h2>Project Delivery</h2>\n<h3>Schedule</h3>\n<div class=\"page-heading\">\n<div class=\"summary-text\">\n<p>The project was paused for approximately three years to resolve legal challenges. Key milestones include: </p>\n</div>\n</div>\n<table border=\"0\" style=\"height: 252px;\">\n<tbody>\n<tr class=\"odd\" style=\"height: 19px;\">\n<td style=\"height: 19px; width: 91px;\">May 2018</td>\n<td style=\"height: 19px; width: 406px;\">City requested proposals (RFP) from qualified consultants</td>\n</tr>\n<tr class=\"even\" style=\"height: 19px;\">\n<td style=\"height: 19px; width: 91px;\">July 2018</td>\n<td style=\"height: 19px; width: 406px;\">City awards contract for preliminary design (Phase 1) to PBS</td>\n</tr>\n<tr class=\"odd\" style=\"height: 48px;\">\n<td style=\"height: 48px; width: 91px;\">Spring 2019</td>\n<td style=\"height: 48px; width: 406px;\">Preliminary design concludes with determination of preferred alternative</td>\n</tr>\n<tr class=\"even\" style=\"height: 19px;\">\n<td style=\"height: 19px; width: 91px;\">March 2019</td>\n<td style=\"height: 19px; width: 406px;\">City acquires property to construct open stream between Shore Lane and Lake Sammamish</td>\n</tr>\n<tr class=\"odd\" style=\"height: 19px;\">\n<td style=\"height: 19px; width: 91px;\">June 2019</td>\n<td style=\"height: 19px; width: 406px;\">City awards contract for permitting and final design (Phase 2) to PBS</td>\n</tr>\n<tr class=\"even\" style=\"height: 19px;\">\n<td style=\"height: 19px; width: 91px;\">2019 - 2022</td>\n<td style=\"height: 19px; width: 406px;\">Initial engineering design, geotechnical investigations, property assessment</td>\n</tr>\n<tr class=\"odd\" style=\"height: 19px;\">\n<td style=\"height: 19px; width: 91px;\">2022-2024</td>\n<td style=\"height: 19px; width: 406px;\">Project paused</td>\n</tr>\n<tr style=\"height: 18px;\">\n<td style=\"height: 18px; width: 91px;\">2025</td>\n<td style=\"height: 18px; width: 406px;\">Final Design, obtain easements and secure permits</td>\n</tr>\n<tr style=\"height: 18px;\">\n<td style=\"height: 18px; width: 91px;\">Feb 2026</td>\n<td style=\"height: 18px; width: 406px;\">Advertise for construction bids</td>\n</tr>\n<tr style=\"height: 18px;\">\n<td style=\"height: 18px; width: 91px;\">June 2026</td>\n<td style=\"height: 18px; width: 406px;\">Begin Construction</td>\n</tr>\n<tr style=\"height: 18px;\">\n<td style=\"height: 18px; width: 91px;\">Q4 2026</td>\n<td style=\"height: 18px; width: 406px;\">Construction substantial completion</td>\n</tr>\n<tr style=\"height: 18px;\">\n<td style=\"height: 18px; width: 91px;\">Q2 2027</td>\n<td style=\"height: 18px; width: 406px;\">Construction final completion</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<h3>Design</h3>\n<p>PBS Engineering and Environmental (an Apex Company) continues to lead the consultant team providing project design work. In December of 2025, PBS provided the City with detailed (100% complete) plans, technical specifications, and an estimate of construction costs.</p>\n<p>This work continued to advance the evolving regulations and direction from the Washington State Department of Fish and Wildlife, and the US Army Corps of Engineers.  In February of 2026, the City put the construction project out to bid and received six bids on the project. In March of 2026, the City formally chose Northwest Construction Inc. as the contractor to construct and restore this project. The Conformed Set of the plans have been posted in the links above, with Volume 1 encompassing the City's portion of the work and Volume 2 encompassing the County's portion of the work. Through an Interagency Agreement with King County, the City was able to package the two projects into one contract to utilize one contractor for the work in the City's and King County's rights-of-way. This allowed the City to provide efficient, cost effective project delivery to our community! </p>\n<h3>Budget</h3>\n<p>Preliminary design efforts cost $90,000. Final design costs are estimated to total approximately $2.2M.  The final engineering estimate on construction cost was approximately $13M, with the lowest, qualified bid on the project of just under $9M.  Property acquisition efforts were concurrent with the design process and were completed in March 2026.</p>\n<p>The City of Sammamish previously paid $4M for property acquisition to rebuild and daylight the stream to Lake Sammamish. Approximately 65% of the purchase price was funded by grants.</p>\n<h3>Grants</h3>\n<p>The George Davis Creek project is receiving extensive financial support through a variety of grant programs. Key partners include:</p>\n<ul>\n<li class=\"odd\"><strong>King County Department of Natural Resources and Parks<br></strong>The County's Land Conservation Initiative is largely supported through the <a rel=\"noopener\" href=\"https://kingcounty.gov/en/dept/dnrp/about-king-county/about-dnrp/grants-partnerships/conservation-futures/overview\" target=\"_blank\">Conservation Futures</a> grant program. Sammamish received a $2,000,000 grant to help purchase property needed for the project.</li>\n<li class=\"odd\"><strong>King County Flood Control District</strong><br>Sammamish receives an annual allocation through the <a rel=\"noopener\" href=\"https://kingcountyfloodcontrol.org/grant-programs-funding/sub-regional-opportunity-fund/\" target=\"_blank\">Subregional Opportunity Fund</a>. Total project allocation to be $1M.</li>\n<li class=\"odd\"><strong>King County Flood Control District</strong><br>The District also dispenses funds through the <a rel=\"noopener\" href=\"https://kingcountyfloodcontrol.org/2024-flood-reduction-grant-program-honoring-steve-bleifuhs-and-advancing-flood-protection/\" target=\"_blank\">Brian Bleifuhs Flood Reduction Grant</a> Program. The City received a $750K grant under this program for construction.</li>\n<li class=\"odd\"><strong>Brian Abbott Fish Barrier Removal Board</strong><br>Sammamish received a $722,350 <a rel=\"noopener\" href=\"https://wdfw.wa.gov/about/advisory/fbrb\" target=\"_blank\">FBRB</a> grant for design costs, and an additional $4.5M for construction. </li>\n<li class=\"odd\"><strong>Washington State Department of Commerce</strong><br>Sammamish received a $500,000 direct capital appropriation for the construction of this project.</li>\n</ul>\n<p>All other project costs will be paid out of the City's Stormwater Capital program that is funded by surface water fees.</p>\n<h3>Project Team</h3>\n<ul>\n<li>Prime Consultant: Apex Companies, LLC (f/k/a PBS Engineering and Environmental)</li>\n<li>Prime Contractor: Northwest Construction Inc</li>\n<li>Stream Analysis and Design: Northwest Hydraulic Consultants</li>\n<li>Real Estate Services: Commonstreet Consulting</li>\n<li>Land Surveying: Apex Engineering, LLC</li>\n<li>Geotechnical Engineering: Aspect Consulting</li>\n<li>Cultural Resources: Stell Environmental</li>\n</ul>\r\n\r\n\r\n itemtype=\"https://schema.org/Article\">\r\n        <header class=\"layout__header content-article-header\">\r\n\r\n<figure id=\"dynamic-key-image\" class=\"key-image\">\r\n    <img\r\n         loading=\"lazy\"\r\n         alt=\"A person stands by a shallow, rocky stream in a wooded area. Work to restore salmon and riparian habitat along the lower reaches of George Davis Creek is a core part of this project. In partnership with King County, this work also includes: </p>\n<p>Replacement of non-fish-passable culverts at East Lake Sammamish Shore Lane Northeast and the King County East Lake Sammamish Trail with new 17-foot box culverts </p>\n<p>Installation a short-span bridge to replace the non-fish-passable culvert under East Lake Sammamish Parkway</p>\n<p>Beginning in May, the City and King County will close a section of the East Lake Sammamish Trail, East Lake Sammamish Parkway, and Shore Lane to replace the aging culverts.</p>\n<p> </p>\r\n\r\n\r\n\r\n        </main>\r\n        \r\n<footer
